---
title: "Monoculture growth"
author: "Shane Hogle"
date: today
---

Inspect the monoculture growth of both Streptomycin-sensitive (Sens/Anc) and Streptomycin-resistant (Res/Evo) forms of *Citrobacter koseri* 1287 and *Pseudomonas chlororaphis* 1977 at different streptomycin concentrations.

These are high resolution growth curves (every 10 minutes) collected on a very nice instrument (Bioscreen). Here we examine how the monoculture growth changed with respect to evolutionary history and streptomycin concentrations

## Growth curves


::: {#fig-01}
![](/figs/bioscreen_strains/growthcurves_monoculture.svg)

Growth curves of *Citrobacter koseri* 1287 (Left column grid) and *Pseudomonas chlororaphis* 1977 (right column grid) at different streptomycin concentrations (grid rows) and evolutionary histories/sensitivities to streptomycin (colors). Each line is a biological replicate (n=5). Growth (culture turbidity) is measured at 10 minute intervals over 48 hours.
:::


## Growth rates

::: {#fig-02}
![](/figs/bioscreen_strains/u_streptomycin_monoculture.svg)

Maximum specific growth rate ($\mathrm{\mu_{max}}$ in $\mathrm{hr^{-1}}$) for the four different bacterial species (panels) and their different evolutionary histories (colors) at different streptomycin concentrations (horizontal axis, μg/ml). Points are the mean over five biological replicates and line ranges show the 95% confidence interval from bootstraps. EVO = experimentally evolved to high streptomycin.
:::
